reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 20. Nay or No: 18. Not Voting: 2. Of 38 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 36 (95%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 208 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

No family should have to choose between paying their bills and finding a safe place to stay when the power goes out. Days without electricity can mean spoiled groceries, lost medication and expensive hotel stays.

That’s why I’m introducing the Power Outage Family Assistance Act https://t.co/djMjjyfc7I

Sam Woll, you are so missed after three years gone. We still think about you. You’ve left an unfillable void, but your legacy of community building and love for others lives on. Thank you for being, as a mutual friend of ours once said, the very best of us. 💙💙 https://t.co/FQ6OmVCmAW

As Co-Chair of the Hostage Task Force, I am deeply grateful that Stephen James Hubbard is returning home to his family after being unjustly held in Russia. We have been fighting for his release for years, and this is good news.

Let me be clear: Vladimir Putin is no “humanitarian.” He invaded Ukraine, killed tens of thousands of Ukrainian soldiers and innocent civilians, and takes American citizens hostage for sport. Just ask Paul Whelan. 

On the heels of going against Congress to give Putin major sanctions relief, the Trump Administration is now praising Putin for an obvious tactic meant to manipulate the President and further pull the U.S. away from aiding Ukraine. Cozying up to Putin and giving him everything he wants is an impending disaster the Ukrainian people—and the world—cannot afford.

Great to visit Oakland County Michigan Works! Last week, I stopped by their new location in Southfield where staff are hard at work helping Michiganders find meaningful employment. They keep our state moving forward! https://t.co/V3jSRV7dtM

The rising trend of hate-filled violence, especially at Houses of Worship, must stop. No American should have to fear for their safety when practicing their faith.

We lowered insulin costs for seniors. Now, we need to lower costs for everyone who relies on lifesaving medications.

Health care should be affordable and accessible for every American. https://t.co/J8IGVdF97N

I keep coming back to is what people did next.

Wixom will always hold a special place in my heart! ❤️

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
